text:
maria: Hey, billing alerted me to a big NAT gateway spike in us-west-e this morning, costs jumped ~3x and I can see a correlated bump in prod GPU node count. anyone tracking?
ashok: Yep noticed it too. Billing graph -> https://billing.example.com/charge/xyz looks like outbound bytes exploded around 09:12.
oliver: Quick check in the gitops repo: prod/network-policy helm values show an override that removed egress restrictions last night. staging still has egress deny.
oliver: ```yaml
# prod override (applied)
networkPolicy:
  enabled: true
  egress: []   # empty -> allows outbound to 0.0.0.0/0
```
gitops-bot: sync status: repo redwood-infra/prod is OUT-OF-SYNC (since 2026-03-18T09:11:04Z). last commit: abc1234 -> applied by pipeline #815.
maria: Wait — how would allowing egress to internet cause GPU scaleups?
jen: Two quick hypotheses: 1) allowing egress made image pulls succeed from public registries causing faster pod restarts and transient burst scale, 2) some init container now talks to an external model puller and spikes startup traffic which the autoscaler interprets as load.
ashok: K8s events show many kubelet/image pull completions and then termination followed by fresh pod scheduling across GPU nodes — repeated restarts for a few deployments. Paste of `kubectl get events` snippet: ```
2026-03-18T09:12:22Z Pod nginx-init BackOff Failed to pull image
2026-03-18T09:12:28Z Pod trainer Created container
2026-03-18T09:13:01Z Pod trainer Started container
```
oliver: Also ran `terraform plan` for prod infra (local dry-run) — saw NGW replacement churn in the plan which lines up with the cost bump: ```
Terraform will perform the following actions:
  ~ aws_eip.nat[0] (forces replacement)
  ~ aws_nat_gateway.ngw[0] (forces replacement)
```
ashok: That replacement explains the NAT bytes but why was networkpolicy changed in the first place? I dug the PR: it was a manual helm value override in the ops team chart to circumvent a broken external dependency (PR #912). The override accidentally removed the egress rules.
maria: Ugh. So manual quick-fix -> opens egress -> side-effect: external model fetch + image churn -> autoscaler spin up GPUs -> big nat cost.
jen: I'm going to propose two immediate mitigations: 1) roll back the helm override to restore egress deny in prod, 2) add an automated parity check that fails CI if prod and staging networkpolicy differ.
sre-oncall: Filing an incident with billing and cost ops, tagging finance. Starting rollback now.
deploy-bot: rollback job started: gitops/apply prod/network-policy revert -> patch 2026-03-18-revert.yaml
deploy-bot: rollback completed: kubectl apply returned success (09:21:05Z).
ashok: Monitoring shows NAT bytes dropping back within 8 minutes, GPU autoscaler stabilized, no new node churn.
maria: Great. Can we also add a guard in the GitOps pipeline to reject manual helm overrides that drop security/routing bits?
jen: Filed INFRA-402: "Prevent accidental egress overrides and add env parity check in CI". Will attach remediation playbook and mock tests.
oliver: I'll open a follow-up PR to add a pre-merge check that diffs prod/staging networkpolicy sets and blocks merges with >0 delta.
maria: Thanks all :thumbsup: Let's keep an eye on the cost alert and close the incident if no regressions in 24h.
